problem: Accessing videos at scale is a daunting engineering endeavor due to their large size and multimodal nature, and evaluating retrieval and generation stages manually is time-consuming (p.2). This work focuses on bringing the context of a large video corpus into the responses of a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chat bot setting (p.2).
methodology: The study proposes using aligned visual caption transcripts, which are temporally synced scene descriptions combining machine-generated visual captions and YouTube subtitles or automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts (p.2). The authors evaluate video summarization using BERTScore (p.2) and test text embeddings against multimodal embeddings (BLIP-2 and CLIP) using 1,000 general knowledge questions to measure retrieval feasibility (p.2-3).
dataset: A dataset of 29,259 public YouTube videos (1.5M video clips, about 215 days of footage) sampled from Panda-70M, augmented with subtitles gathered from YouTube's APIs (p.2).
results: Text embeddings using aligned transcripts and ASR achieved higher HIT@K and QUALITY@1 scores at lower K compared to cross-modal text-to-vision match embeddings like BLIP-2 and CLIP (p.3). Specifically, text-embedding-3-small on aligned transcripts scored 0.741 for HIT@1, 0.934 for HIT@5, 0.971 for HIT@10, and 7.377 for QUALITY@1 (p.3).
key_findings: Aligned visual captions produce summary quality comparable to multimodal LLMs while avoiding the need to send entire sets of video frames, significantly saving on context windows and processing bandwidth (p.2). Text embeddings over aligned transcripts are highly feasible for video retrieval augmented generation, finding relevant hits at low K values (p.3).
limitations: Practical considerations include the availability of video captioning models suitable for the intended use case and the challenge of identifying meaningful video clip segments to be summarized (p.4). Additionally, the audio signal incorporated focuses only on the spoken word rather than other audio aspects like music or loudness shifts (p.5).
title: Video Enriched Retrieval Augmented Generation Using Aligned Video Captions
